problems.stem: Which slide choice passes a basic accessibility check?
options: Light gray (#BBBBBB) body text on a white (#FFFFFF) background.
Dark navy (#1A2A4F) text on white, alt text on every chart, and status shown by label plus color not color alone.
Red and green status dots with no labels.
A chart image with no alt text because it 'looks self-explanatory'.
problems.explanation: Strong contrast, alt text, and non-color-only encoding together meet the core accessibility requirements.

problems.stem: Which note gives BigAL a concrete accessibility fault to fix?
options: Is this accessible?
My slide marks 'on track' green and 'at risk' red with only dots, so a colorblind viewer cannot tell them apart. How should I label them?
Make it accessible.
I think it is fine.
problems.explanation: The note names a specific color-only encoding problem so feedback can target a labeling fix.

problems.stem: What is a sound boundary for using AI on accessibility?
options: Ask AI to declare the deck accessible and skip checking.
Ask AI to draft alt text for each chart, then verify each draft actually matches what the chart shows.
Let AI pick any color theme without checking contrast.
Avoid AI and also skip the manual contrast check.
problems.explanation: AI can draft alt text, but you must verify it describes the real image and still confirm contrast yourself.

problems.stem: A reviewer flags 'low contrast' on your title. Which revision is the real fix?
options: Make the title font larger but keep it light gray.
Darken the title color until it reaches at least a 4.5:1 contrast ratio against the background.
Add an animation to the title.
Center the title.
problems.explanation: Contrast is fixed by adjusting the color values to meet the ratio, not by resizing or animating the text.

problems.stem: Your 40pt slide title is a light color and you want to verify its contrast. Which WCAG AA threshold applies?
options: 4.5:1, the same as body text.
3:1, the large-text threshold (text 18pt and up, or 14pt bold).
No threshold; large text is exempt from contrast checks.
7:1, because titles matter more.
problems.explanation: WCAG AA sets 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text, defined as 18pt and up (or 14pt bold). A 40pt title is large text, so 3:1 applies; that is a lower bar, not an exemption, and a pale title can still fail it. (7:1 is the AAA normal-text level, not the AA title rule.)
